title: MicroservicePrd:Slides

_meta.purpose: Slides microservice PRD/source-authority lock for workplace presentation authoring, collaboration, present/broadcast, import/export, accessibility, ACL, versioning, and intelligence-assisted design/content. This source map uses oya/slides/manifest.json and the slides source-lock artifact as provenance, but it does not treat inventory, stale legacy paths, or existing service-home artifacts as runtime or product-readiness evidence.

user_stories.story: As an employee deck author, I can create, open, save, rename, duplicate, delete, and restore decks so that presentation work remains durable and versioned.

As a deck author, I can add and edit slides, text boxes, shapes, tables, equations, images, videos, audio, themes, templates, master slides, and slide sorter ordering so that rich presentations can be authored without leaving Oyatie.
As collaborators, multiple users can edit the same deck with cursor presence, CRDT conflict surfacing, comments, suggestions, and no silent data loss.
As a presenter, I can enter present mode and optionally broadcast through the messenger LiveKit boundary while viewers see degraded-state messaging instead of silent failure.
As a deck owner, I can import PPTX, ODP, Keynote, and PDF files and export PPTX, ODP, PDF/PDF-A, PNG-per-slide, and MP4 artifacts through sandboxed, policy-gated jobs.

As a keyboard or assistive-technology user, I can navigate and present decks with semantic objects, reading order, alt-text, contrast checks, reduced-motion support, and an accessibility bridge for Canvas/WebGL fallback.
As a deck owner, I can set deck-level and per-slide ACLs, share restricted links, preview Cedar effects before changing access, and prevent public-link or export egress when policy forbids it.
As a reviewer or records officer, I can inspect version history, restore versions, and trace share/export/ACL/AI events into immutable audit evidence.

As a deck author, I can ask for T0/T1/T2 design, content, and accessibility assistance with human-review, risk-class, provenance, watermark, and refusal semantics handled through intelligence boundaries.

As an integrator, I can use sheets chart links, drive media/assets, messenger broadcast, social/community publishing, mail notifications, identity principals, and intelligence assistance through explicit contracts without assuming those sibling services are already ready.

processing_boundaries: Deck content, comments, version history, imports, exports, and AI prompt/output data remain tenant-scoped product data, not governance evidence payloads.

DPIA automation evidence may include identifiers, decision ids, verifier run ids, status URLs, ArgoCD sync ids, governance lane ids, and audit-chain references, but it must not copy tenant payload, PHI, payment-card data, message bodies, document bodies, or secrets into governance evidence.
Export/import jobs must enforce malware scanning, sandboxing, egress policy, retention/legal hold, and jurisdiction pack constraints before output release.
AI assistance records must retain provenance/watermark/risk-class metadata and human-review state for regulated contexts.
retention_and_legal_hold: Decks, slides, comments, version history, share/ACL events, import/export jobs, and audit-chain pointers are retained per tenant pack and legal-hold policy.
Legal hold preserves deck content, version history, export job lineage, share-link changes, and AI provenance even when normal retention expires.
Access/export requests receive scoped projections rather than raw audit-chain mutation or payload leakage.
regulatory_notes: EU: GDPR storage limitation, data-subject access/export, cross-border transfer, and AI-risk disclosure for content generation.
KR: PIPA-compatible retention, pack-localized export/egress controls, and Korean input/search/accessibility evidence where applicable.
US and US-healthcare: employment discovery, HIPAA overlays when PHI is embedded, and audit/eDiscovery packet integrity.
PCI-DSS applicability is limited to cases where payment/card artifacts are embedded or exported; slides must not claim card-processing scope by default.

authn_authz: OIDC bearer identity for API access
tenant_id and pack scoping on every deck/slide/import/export/broadcast operation
deck-level and per-slide ACLs with Cedar-preview before access-expanding mutations
auditor and regulator roles use scoped read/export projections, never implicit edit rights
policy_guardrails: Public links are restricted by tenant policy and cannot bypass pack, retention, legal-hold, or export controls.
Export/egress is refused when pack policy, malware verdict, legal hold, or data-class rules block release.
Canvas/WebGL fallback cannot remove accessibility semantics or policy hooks from the canonical slide model.
AI T2 content generation requires provenance, risk-class, policy evaluation, and human-review semantics where required.
Broadcast viewer identities may be pseudonymized for audience interactions but presenter/admin/audit identity remains traceable.
secrets_and_sandbox: OpenBao-style secret references remain pointers only; secrets are never embedded in this source map or governance evidence.
Import/export workers run in sandboxed conversion pools and must not execute tenant-provided code outside approved conversion primitives.
CRDT session HMAC keys are session scoped and never logged.

ai_automation_bounds.intelligence_boundary: All model/capability execution, risk classification, evaluation, provenance, watermarking, and refusal semantics route through intelligence. Slides owns deck UX, policy preview, persistence, and audit linkage; it does not own model runtime authority.
ai_automation_bounds.retired_dependency_rewrite: Any legacy Foundry wording in manifest/proto/source artifacts is historical/provenance or comments only; active scope must say intelligence and must not revive a Foundry service/runtime.
eu_ai_act_notes: AI design suggestions and alt-text suggestions are usually low/medium risk when user-reviewed.
T2 content generation in employment, educational, legal, medical, credit, or similarly consequential contexts requires high-risk policy review, human oversight, provenance, and refusal paths.
Exported decks that include AI-generated content must preserve visible or inspectable provenance/watermark metadata according to tenant and jurisdiction policy.
